title: Change detection using Landsat time series: A review of frequencies, preprocessing, algorithms, and applications
source: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing 130, 370-384
relevance: Organizes change detection by OBSERVATION FREQUENCY - bi-temporal, multi-temporal, and dense annual/sub-annual trajectory methods - and makes explicit which algorithm families each frequency supports. That is the map we needed to place ourselves: 18 irregular acquisitions over 24 years with 2-4 year gaps sits below the density that trajectory fitting (LandTrendr, CCDC, BFAST) assumes, so the honest reading is that our series supports EPOCH-PAIR comparison rather than trajectory reconstruction. Use it to justify the design choice rather than defaulting to whichever algorithm is fashionable.

authors: Zhang, L., Rupnik, E. & Pierrot-Deseilligny, M.
title: Feature matching for multi-epoch historical aerial images
source: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing 182, 176-189
relevance: Solves the specific problem that gates every per-crown change claim we want to make: matching features BETWEEN EPOCHS of historical aerial imagery, where radiometry, sensor and scene have all changed. Our Phase 3 Search 7 covered the CONSEQUENCES of misregistration (IDs 21-26); this is the method for reducing it across exactly our kind of archive, and the fine-scale tree-loss literature names multi-temporal misalignment as its dominant error source. Directly applicable to aligning the 2000/2002 King acquisitions to the modern era, where co-registration is worst and our recall is lowest.
